comment: I mapped small molecules (sorafenib, GTP, GDP, EGF) as chemicals; unmodified proteins to their canonical gene/protein names (RAF1 = C-RAF, BRAF = B-RAF, MEK family = MAP2K1/MAP2K2, ERK family = MAPK1/MAPK3, GRB2, SOS1/2, EGFR). RAS family instances are expanded to HRAS/KRAS/NRAS and when nucleotide-bound (Ras_GTP, Ras_GDP) treated as protein–ligand complexes (RAS + GTP/GDP). Inhibitor-bound RAF species (iRaf1, iBRaf, nfpi*, nfp*) and tetramers/dimers are represented as complexes composed of the underlying RAF proteins (RAF1 and/or BRAF), RAS proteins where present, and sorafenib as the ligand. EGFR-related species (mE, mEL, mELmEL, E, EG2, EG2SOS, GRB2_SOS) are mapped to EGFR (ERBB1) and its complexes with EGF, GRB2 and SOS; GRB2_SOS and EG2SOS are multi-protein complexes containing GRB2 and SOS bound to EGFR. Modified forms (pRaf1, pMEK, pERK, nfp*, nfpi*) are mapped to the base protein names (RAF1, MAP2K1/2, MAPK1/3, RAF1/BRAF, SOS) while treating the species as protein or protein-containing complexes per their reactions. Multiplicities and phosphorylation state were not listed as separate component names (components are the standardized proteins/chemicals present).
